s7001_PP_o2: Yes, "on" is right! We use on with days, like Saturday. Now try a new one. Write in, on or at: "My birthday is ___ June."
s7004_PP_o2: Yes, "on" is right! We use on with days, like Tuesday. Now try a new one. Write in, on or at: "The film starts ___ 8 o'clock."
s7007_PP_o2: You are doing well, and this one is hard, so let's do it together. Look at the sentence: "My best teacher is Mr Ali." Let's change one part. Write a full sentence about your favourite animal. Start with "My favourite animal is ..."
s7010_PP_o2: Yes, "an" is right! Umbrella starts with a vowel sound, so we use an. Now try a new one. Write a or the: "I have a book. ___ book is new."
s7013_PP_o2: Good try, you used all the right words! But the order is not correct. In English the subject comes first. Hint: who makes the tea? Start with "My aunt". Also, often goes before the main verb. Try again: "often / my aunt / tea / makes"
s7016_PP_o2: Let's do the spelling together. The word is k-i-t-c-h-e-n. After the h there is an e, then n. Say it slowly: kit-chen. Now type the whole word: "I make toast in the ___."
s7019_PP_o2: Yes, "on" is right! We use on with days, like Tuesday. Now try a new one. Write in, on or at: "The film starts ___ 8 o'clock."
s7022_PP_o2: Well done! You wrote a capital W, a capital L for London, and a full stop at the end. Names of cities always start with a capital letter. Now write your own sentence. Tell me where you live. Start with a capital letter and end with a full stop.
s7025_PP_o2: Yes, "We usually have lunch." is right! The order is subject, then usually, then the verb and the object. Usually goes before the main verb, have. Now try the last one. Put in order: "often / my aunt / tea / makes"
s7028_PP_o2: Yes, "an" is right! Umbrella starts with a vowel sound, so we use an. Now try a new one. Write a or the: "I have a book. ___ book is new."
s7031_PP_o2: Very good! "My teacher is kind. She is tall." Each sentence starts with a capital letter, has is, and ends with a full stop. Now write 2 sentences about your neighbour. Use is or has in each sentence.
s7034_PP_o2: Yes, "I am happy because it is my birthday." is right! Because gives the reason in the same sentence. Now write your own. Join with because: "I am tired. I work all day."
s7037_PP_o2: Very good! "I would like a glass of water, please." is polite, and you used I would like and please. Now a new situation. You are in a shop and you want a bottle of juice. Ask politely with "Can I have ..." and add please.
s7040_PP_o2: Yes, "She always gets up early." is right! Always goes before the main verb, gets. Now try a new one. Rewrite this sentence with never: "My brother eats breakfast."
s7043_PP_o2: Good! "I am going to visit my aunt." has am going to plus a verb. But a plan needs a future time word. Hint: add tomorrow, next week or on Friday at the end. Try again: write the sentence with a future time.
s7046_PP_o2: Yes, many is right! We can count bottles, so we use many: "How many bottles are there?" Now try a new one. Write a few or a little: "I have ___ rice left, only a spoonful."
s7049_PP_o2: Very good! "Excuse me, which platform does the train to the coast leave from?" is a polite question, and does comes before the subject. Now a new task. You want to borrow a pen from your friend. Ask politely with "Could I borrow ... please?"
s7052_PP_o2: Yes, watches is right! Watch ends in -ch, so with she we add -es. Now try a new one. Write the correct form: "The baby ___ (cry) at night." Answer with only the verb.
s7055_PP_o2: Very good! "He is funny." is a correct sentence about personality, and you used is with an adjective. Now try describing someone you know. Write two sentences about your friend: one about hair or eyes, and one about personality.
s7058_PP_o2: Yes, "He has short black hair." is right! The adjectives come before hair. Now write the second sentence: tell me about the actor's personality. Use "He is ..." and one word like kind or funny.
s7061_PP_o2: Yes, "more expensive" is right! Expensive is a long word, so we use more and not -er. Now try a new one. Complete: "A bus is ___ (slow) than a train." Remember to use than.
s7064_PP_o2: Good try, but "tell me" is a blunt command, so it can sound rude. Hint: use a question frame. Start with "Excuse me, which platform ..." and use does before the train. Try again: ask which platform the train to the coast leaves from.
s7067_PP_o2: Yes, "How much are these socks?" is right! Socks is more than one thing, so we use are. Now try a new one. You want a hat in a different colour. Ask the shop assistant with "Do you have this hat in ...?" and a colour.
s7070_PP_o2: Very good! "I am going to visit my friend tomorrow." is a correct plan. You used am going to plus a verb, and tomorrow is a future time. Now a new one. Tell me a plan for next week. Use "We are going to ..." and a verb like study, visit or play.
